metadata.title: Murray (1981) Thomas Substrate-Inhibition Reaction-Diffusion Pre-Pattern & Conical Tail Eigenmode Transition Reference Dataset

sources.citation: Murray JD (1981). A pre-pattern formation mechanism for animal coat markings. Journal of Theoretical Biology 88(1):161-199.
Thomas D (1975). Artificial enzyme membranes: transport, memory, and oscillations. Biochimie 57(4):499-507.
Murray JD (1988). How the leopard gets its spots. Scientific American 258(3):80-87.
Liu RT, Liaw SS, Maini PK (2006). Two-stage Turing model for generating pigment patterns on the leopard and the jaguar. Physical Review E 74(1):011914.

panthera_pardus_kruger.species: Panthera pardus pardus (African leopard, adult lateral profile with rosetted flank and banded distal tail)
panthera_pardus_kruger.author: Bernard DUPONT (Kruger National Park, South Africa)

governing_pde.u_eq: du/dt = gamma * (a - u - rho*u*v / (1 + u + K*u^2)) + Lap(u)
governing_pde.v_eq: dv/dt = gamma * (alpha*(b - v) - rho*u*v / (1 + u + K*u^2)) + d * Lap(v)
governing_pde.boundary_condition: Zero-flux (Neumann) n . grad(u) = n . grad(v) = 0 on domain boundary

conical_tail_eigenmode_transition.theorem_statement: A spotted animal can have a striped (ringed) tail, but a striped animal cannot have a spotted tail.

tapered_cylinder_geometry.effective_wavenumber_formula: k_{n,m}^2(r) = (n * pi / L)^2 + (m / r)^2 in [gamma * k_-^2, gamma * k_+^2]

scale_gamma_regimes.description: Domain scale gamma too small to fit even the n=1 fundamental mode inside [gamma*k_-^2, gamma*k_+^2]

scale_gamma_regimes.species_example: Acinonyx jubatus / Felis catus distal tail
scale_gamma_regimes.description: Circumferential m>=1 modes exceed upper Turing cutoff; pure axial m=0 stripes/rings dominate

scale_gamma_regimes.species_example: Panthera pardus / Panthera onca tapered tail
scale_gamma_regimes.description: Broad proximal tail base (r > r_crit) supports m>=1 spots; narrow distal tip (r < r_crit) supports only m=0 rings
Multiple 2D (nx, ny) eigenmodes unstable across both axial and circumferential axes
Very large scale factor gamma crowds many high-order modes, approaching fine-scale or uniform appearance
